title: DCASE 2026 Task 2 Official Results and Technical Reports
authors: DCASE 2026 Task 2 organizers and participating teams
key_finding: The official result collection shows a broad performance frontier built from heterogeneous encoders, scoring backends, stereo views, calibration rules, and ensembles, with large machine-dependent variation.
audit_relationship: Defines the contemporary comparison set and prevents CARE-ASD from treating ordinary score fusion, stereo processing, or multi-backend ensembling as a new contribution.

title: DCASE 2026 Challenge Submission and Technical Report Policy
key_finding: The official policy distinguishes challenge technical reports from peer-reviewed workshop publications and fixes how system evidence must be described.
audit_relationship: Requires every DCASE technical report in this delta to be treated as a current primary system description rather than peer-reviewed scientific confirmation.

title: Scoring Backends Matter More Than Pooling: A Systematic Study of Training-Free Anomalous Sound Detection under Domain Shift
key_finding: Backend choice moves target-domain AUC much more than temporal pooling; train-normal z-normalized minimum fusion nearly closes the per-machine oracle gap, while proxy-outlier pseudo-validation fails because candidates saturate.
audit_relationship: Directly argues against another pooling search and warns that the pseudo-fault selection signal used to motivate expert choice can be uninformative even when candidate backends differ on real anomalies.

title: Training-Free Model Selection and Domain-Aware Score Calibration for First-Shot Anomalous Sound Detection
key_finding: A cross-validated normal-only domain-balance criterion predicts DCASE 2025 evaluation ranking better than development score, but can select degenerate maps unless paired with a coarse labeled-development viability veto.
audit_relationship: Makes domain calibration and label-free selection mandatory comparators, while prohibiting claims that a normal-only criterion alone establishes anomaly-detection power or cross-year transfer.

title: Cross-Channel and Raw-Spectral Detector Ensembles for First-Shot Noise-Aware Anomalous Sound Detection
key_finding: A ridge predictor of far-channel embeddings from near-channel embeddings supplies a predictive-consistency residual, while a separate raw-log-mel Mahalanobis detector adds representation diversity beyond the embedding density core.
audit_relationship: Shows that cross-channel predictive residuals and raw-spectral rescue are prior art; a successor can use them only as comparators or contribute a distinct safety, identifiability, or transfer test.

title: Noise-Aware First-Shot Unsupervised Anomalous Sound Detection via Frozen Encoders, Wiener Denoising, and Shiftall-LDKNN Scoring
authors: Yasaman Shokriazar; Arian Moradi; Felix Leber; Alfiia Ziganshina
key_finding: Frozen BEATs and EAT views, Wiener denoising, raw near-minus-far audio, LDKNN, and train-only source-to-target mean-shift augmentation are fused with weights assessed by strict leave-one-machine-out validation.
audit_relationship: Provides a strong existing multi-view route and a leakage-conscious LOMO protocol, making approximate reconstruction expensive and scientifically weak unless CARE-ASD isolates a new mechanism.

title: A Train-Normal Profile Ensemble for Noise-Aware Unsupervised Anomalous Sound Detection
key_finding: A broad normal-profile component bank compares consensus, top-tail rescue, two-sided rank, and agreement-balanced aggregation; the reported development replay favors domain consensus over top-tail rescue.
audit_relationship: Removes sparse top-tail rescue as a novel immediate response to V10 and supplies direct counterevidence against assuming that sparse expert activation should improve the official score.

title: AITHU Submission for DCASE 2026 Task 2: Robust Machine-Wise Scoring with BEATs Representations
authors: Anbai Jiang; Xinhu Zheng; Wenrui Liang; Shuwei Zhang; Tianyu Liu; Jia Liu; Pingyi Fan; Wei-Qiang Zhang; Cheng Lu; Xie Chen; Yanmin Qian
key_finding: Heterogeneous BEATs scoring branches, independent training seeds, and generative augmentation are selected and fused at score level, with a reported development harmonic mean of 68.20 percent.
audit_relationship: Shows that generic complementarity and BEATs score fusion are already crowded prior art and that competitive systems use diversity beyond the three correlated fixed branches tested by V10.

title: N-1 Experts: Unsupervised Anomaly Detection Model Selection
authors: Constantin Le Clei; Yasha Pushak; Fatjon Zogaj; Moein Owhadi-Kareshk; Zahra Zohrevand; Robert Harlow; Hesam Fathi Moghadam; Sungpack Hong; Hassan Chafi
key_finding: Candidate anomaly detectors can be ranked by agreement with a panel of other detectors without labeled target data, under an assumption that detector errors and anomaly definitions are sufficiently diverse.
audit_relationship: Establishes adjacent prior art for agreement-based unsupervised model selection and exposes the diversity assumption that V10's uniformly inactive expert family does not satisfy.
